gap: No result ChatGPT got turns the scanners' stated volumetric accuracy into error over a real part length. At 1 m the EinScan Rigil's Laser HD spec (0.04 + 0.06 mm/m) works out to ±0.10 mm, and its IR Rapid spec (0.1 + 0.4 mm/m) to ±0.50 mm. The FreeScan UE Pro2 with photogrammetry (0.02 + 0.015 mm/m) works out to ±0.035 mm. That puts the Rigil's laser mode exactly at the '±0.1 mm mechanical fit' limit that ChatGPT's own filter offers, its IR mode far past it, and the UE Pro2 about 3× tighter.
standout_why: I compared against the cited invenio3d.com.au buyer's guide, the cited trimechmanufacturing.com SHINING 3D 2026 guide and 3dscannermatch.com's reverse-engineering page. invenio3d gives only headline figures ('0.02mm' UE Pro, 'up to ±0.025mm' BLACK Elite) and says large parts raise 'cumulative alignment errors' without putting a number on it. TriMech gives no accuracy figure for the Rigil or UE Pro2 and calls volumetric accuracy 'accuracy over longer distances' with no numbers. 3dscannermatch gives no accuracy numbers at all. None of them separates per-frame from volumetric accuracy, works the mm/m formula out at any part length, or notes which spec cites a test standard. ChatGPT's own answer puts per-frame or point figures (Creaform 'up to 0.030 mm', MetroX Pro '0.02 mm per frame') next to the Rigil's volumetric '0.04 mm + 0.06 mm/m' as if they could be compared.
decides: This confirms the higher tier and sharpens the middle one. For parts around 1 m that need ±0.05 mm or better, only the UE Pro2 with photogrammetry meets it on its stated spec (±0.035 mm). The Rigil should only be recommended in Laser HD mode for ±0.1 mm work, and its IR Rapid mode (±0.30 mm at 500 mm) is shape-capture only. The budget picks (MetroX, MetroX Pro, Raptor, Raptor Pro) can only be placed once their mm/m figures come from the maker. Creality's US store pages publish no accuracy figure at all, so the page can't quote one from the store.

findings.value: up to 0.04 mm + 0.06 mm/m (±0.07 mm at 0.5 m; ±0.10 mm at 1 m)
findings.note: Same for the 32 GB and 24 GB versions. Arithmetic: 0.04 + 0.06 × L(m). The page gives no single-frame figure and names no test standard (no VDI/VDE 2634 or ISO 10360), unlike the UE Pro2.

findings.label: Volumetric accuracy, IR Rapid mode
findings.value: up to 0.1 mm + 0.4 mm/m (±0.30 mm at 0.5 m; ±0.50 mm at 1 m)
findings.note: Arithmetic: 0.1 + 0.4 × L(m). At 1 m the error is 5× the Laser HD figure, so the 'blue-laser and infrared modes' ChatGPT promoted are not two equal options for reverse engineering.
